a19.salok: Salok. Nothing goes along with you but the worship of God; all the poison of worldly vice is ashes. Earning the Naam, the Name of the Lord, Har Har: Nanak, this is the wealth of real worth.
a19.p1: Ashtapadi. Meet with the saints and reflect together. Remember the One, and make the Naam your support. Put all other efforts out of your mind, my friend; keep the lotus feet of the Lord enshrined in your heart. That God is all-powerful, the doer and the cause of all. Hold firmly to the merchandise of the Lord's Name. Gather this wealth and be fortunate; this is the pure teaching of the saints. Keep your hope in the One alone, within your mind. Nanak, all your ills will then be cured.
a19.p2: The wealth for which you rise and run to the four corners of the earth, that wealth you will find by serving the Lord. The peace you long for every day, my friend, that peace lies in love for the company of the holy. The honour for which you do good deeds, for that honour, hurry to the Lord's refuge. The illness does not go with countless remedies; the illness is cured when the medicine of the Lord is applied. Of all treasures, the treasure is the Lord's Name. Repeat it, Nanak, and be accepted in the Lord's Court.
a19.p3: Awaken the mind through the Lord's Name; running in the ten directions, it comes back to rest in its place. No obstacle troubles the one in whose heart that Lord dwells. This dark age of Kali is burning hot; the Lord's Name is cool. Remember it again and again, and have peace for ever. Fear is destroyed and hope is fulfilled; through loving devotion the soul is lit from within. In that heart the Imperishable Lord comes to dwell. Says Nanak, death's noose is cut.
a19.p4: The true devotee states this essential truth: whoever keeps being born and dying is unripe, utterly unripe. Coming and going in birth and death ends by serving God: give up self-conceit and take refuge with the divine Guru. In this way the jewel of human birth is redeemed; remember the Lord, Har Har, the mainstay of life. No one is released by countless efforts, nor by pondering the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas. Worship the Lord with your mind fixed on him. Nanak, you will receive the fruit your heart desires.
a19.p5: Your wealth will not go along with you; why do you cling to it, foolish mind? Sons, friends, family and wife: tell me, which of them will be your protector? Kingly power, pleasures and the vast spread of Maya, the world's illusion: tell me, who has ever been freed by these? Horses, elephants and riding in chariots are a false pomp, a false display. The ignorant one does not recognise him who gave all this; forgetting the Naam, Nanak, he comes to regret.
a19.p6: Take the Guru's teaching, ignorant one; without devotion many clever people have drowned. Worship the Lord with devotion, my mind, my friend, and your consciousness will become pure. Keep his lotus feet in your mind, and the sins of birth after birth will leave. Repeat the Naam yourself and have others repeat it; by hearing it, speaking it and living by it you will reach liberation. The Lord's Name is the very essence, the truth. Sing his praises, Nanak, in poise and natural love.
a19.p7: Singing his praises, your filth will be washed away, and the spreading poison of ego will be destroyed. You will be free of care and live in peace; hold the Lord's Name dear with each breath and each morsel. Give up all your cleverness, my mind; in the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy, the true wealth will be yours. Gather the capital of the Lord and trade with it; here you will have peace, and in the Lord's Court acclaim. See the One alone within all. Says Nanak, this comes to the one on whose forehead it is written.
a19.p8: Repeat the One alone, praise the One alone. Remember the One, and long, my mind, for the One alone. Sing the endless praises of the One. With mind and body repeat the one Lord's Name. The Lord himself is the One, the One alone. God is fully pervading, filling all. The countless expanses of creation came from the One. Worshipping the One, sins have gone. Mind and body are dyed deep within in the colour of the one God. By the Guru's grace, Nanak, the One has been known.
a20.salok: Salok. Wandering and wandering, God, I have come and fallen into your refuge. This is Nanak's prayer, God: attach me to your devotion.
a20.p1: Ashtapadi. Your servant, a beggar, begs God for a gift: in your grace, Lord, grant me your Name. I beg for the dust of the holy ones' feet. Supreme Lord, fulfil my longing: may I sing God's praises for ever and ever; with every breath, God, may I meditate on you. May love for your lotus feet take hold of me; may I worship God with devotion day after day. You alone are my shelter and my support. Nanak asks for God's Name, the most excellent of all.
a20.p2: By God's glance of grace comes great peace. Only a rare one finds the sweet essence of the Lord. Those who have tasted it are content; they are complete beings, and they do not waver. They are filled to the brim with the joy and colour of love; in the company of the holy, longing for him wells up. Giving up all else, they have fallen into his refuge; within them is light, and night and day their minds are fixed on him. By great fortune they have meditated on that God. Nanak, imbued with the Naam, God's Name, one is at peace.
a20.p3: The servant's wish has been fulfilled; from the True Guru he has received pure understanding. God has become merciful to his servant and has made him joyful for ever. His bonds are cut and the servant is free; the pain of birth and death and all doubt are gone. His desire is met, his longing wholly fulfilled; he sees the Lord pervading all, ever with him, ever present. He to whom he belonged has united him with himself. Nanak, through devotion he merges in the Naam.
a20.p4: How can he be forgotten, who does not let our toil go to waste? How can he be forgotten, who acknowledges what is done for him? How can he be forgotten, who has given us everything? How can he be forgotten, who is the life of all beings? How can he be forgotten, who keeps us safe in the fire? By the Guru's grace only a rare one perceives this. How can he be forgotten, who draws us out of poison, and joins again those parted from him for lifetimes? The perfect Guru has made this essential truth clear. Nanak, his servants have meditated on their God.
a20.p5: Friends, saints, do this work: give up all else and repeat the Name of the Lord. Remember, remember, remember him, and find peace. Repeat the Naam yourselves and have others repeat it. Through loving devotion the world-ocean is crossed; without devotion the body will turn to ashes. The Naam is the treasure of every blessing and comfort; even one who is drowning finds rest in it. Every sorrow is destroyed. Nanak, repeat the Naam of the Lord, the treasure of virtues.
a20.p6: Love has welled up in me, the sweetness of love, and longing; within mind and body this alone is my aim: to behold his sight with my eyes and be at peace. The mind blossoms as it washes the feet of the holy. The devotees are dyed in his love, mind and body; only a rare one gains their company. Be merciful and give me one thing: that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam. His praise cannot be told. Nanak, he is present in all.
a20.p7: God is forgiving, merciful to the meek. He loves his devotees and is ever kind. He is Master of the masterless, Gobind, Gopal, sustainer of the world; he cherishes every heart. He is the Primal Being, the cause of all, the Creator, the mainstay of his devotees' lives. Whoever repeats his Name becomes pure, fixing the mind's love on him in loving devotion. We are without virtue, lowly and ignorant. Nanak is in your refuge, Lord, Supreme Being.
a20.p8: All the heavens, freedom and liberation are gained by singing the Lord's praises for a single moment. Many kingdoms, pleasures and honours belong to one whose mind delights in the telling of the Lord's Name. Many foods, garments and music are his whose tongue repeats Har Har every day. Good are his deeds, glorious and rich is he in whose heart dwells the perfect Guru's teaching. God, let me dwell in the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy. Nanak, there every comfort shines forth.
a21.salok: Salok. He himself has qualities and is beyond qualities; he is the Formless One, absorbed in the trance of the void (sunn samadhi). Nanak, he himself made all this, and he himself, in turn, meditates on himself.
a21.p1: Ashtapadi. When none of this visible world could be seen, where then could sin and merit come from? When he himself had entered his own trance of the void, then with whom could anyone practise hatred and strife? When the world had no colour or mark to be seen, then tell me, whom could joy and grief take hold of? When the Supreme Lord was all alone, by himself, then where was attachment, and who could have doubt? He himself has set his own play in motion. Nanak, there is no other doer.
a21.p2: When God the Master alone existed, then tell me, who could be counted bound or free? When there was only the Lord, unreachable and infinite, then tell me, who could be born into hell or heaven? When God was beyond qualities, in his own natural poise, then tell me, where were Shiva and Shakti, spirit and matter? When he kept his own light within himself, then who was without fear, and who feared what? He himself performs his own wondrous plays. Nanak, the Master is unreachable and infinite.
a21.p3: When the Imperishable was seated at ease in his own place, then tell me, where were birth, death and destruction? When there was only that perfect Creator God, then tell me, who could feel the terror of death? When God, unmanifest and beyond the senses, was the One alone, then of whom could Chitra and Gupta, the recorders of deeds, ask an account? When the Master was stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable, then who was set free, and who was tied in bonds? He himself, by himself, is the wonder. Nanak, he himself brought forth his own form.
a21.p4: Where there was only the pure Being, the Lord of all beings, there was no filth; tell me, what was there to wash? Where there was only the stainless, formless One, free of all desire, there who had honour, and who had pride? Where the Lord of the world was present in his own form alone, there, tell me, whom could deceit and fault cling to? Where the One whose being is light was merged in his own light, there who was hungry, and who could be satisfied? He is the doer, the cause of all doing, the Creator. Nanak, the Creator is beyond all reckoning.
a21.p5: When he had made his glory with himself alone, then who was mother, father, friend, son or brother? Where he himself was master of every power, there where were the Vedas and the Katebs (the Semitic scriptures), and who was there to recognise them? When he held himself within himself, then who could weigh good omens and bad? Where he himself was the high and himself the near, there who could be called master, and who servant? We are lost in wonder upon wonder, amazed. Nanak, you alone know your own state.
a21.p6: Where the One who cannot be deceived, pierced or divided was absorbed in himself, there whom could Maya, the world's illusion, take hold of? He bowed in homage to himself alone; the three qualities of Maya had no entry there. Where there was only the One, the one Lord alone, there who was free of care, and who could be touched by care? Where he himself was content within himself, there who was to speak, and who to listen? He is vast and endless, higher than the highest. Nanak, he alone can reach himself.
a21.p7: When he himself fashioned the visible expanse of the world, he spread it out within the three qualities. Then came talk of sin and merit; one is bound for hell, another longs for heaven. The snares of household life and the entanglements of Maya, the burdens of ego, attachment, doubt and fear, pain and pleasure, honour and dishonour: all these came to be told of in many ways. He himself stages his own play and watches it. When he winds up the play, Nanak, then he alone remains.
a21.p8: Where the devotee of the Unmanifest is, there he himself is. Where he spreads out the expanse of creation, it is for the glory of his saints. He himself is the Master of both sides; his glory befits him alone. He himself performs his plays, his joyful wonders; he himself enjoys every pleasure and yet remains untouched. Whom he pleases, he attaches to his Name; whom he pleases, he makes play the game of the world. He is beyond count, fathomless, numberless and beyond weighing. As you make him speak, so your servant Nanak speaks.
a22.salok: Salok. Master of every being and creature, you yourself are present and at work in all. Nanak, the One alone is spread out everywhere; where is any other to be seen?
a22.p1: Ashtapadi. He himself speaks, and he himself is the one who listens. He himself is the One, and he himself the vast expanse. When it pleases him, he brings forth the creation; by his own will he draws it back into himself. Nothing is apart from you; on your own thread you have strung the whole world. The one whom God himself gives understanding, that servant receives the true Name. He looks on all alike and knows the essence of reality. Nanak, he is the conqueror of the whole world.
a22.p2: All beings and creatures rest in his hands; merciful to the meek, he is the Master of the masterless. One whom he protects, no one can kill; that one is dead whom he puts out of his mind. Forsaking him, where else can one go? Above every head is the one stainless King. He in whose hand lie all the ways of every being, know him to be with you, within and without. He is the treasure of virtues, endless and infinite. His servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him.
a22.p3: The merciful Lord is fully pervading everywhere; he is kind to all. He himself knows his own doings; the knower of hearts pervades all. He cherishes his beings in many ways; whatever he has created meditates on him. Whom he pleases, he unites with himself; they worship him, singing the Lord's praises. With faith in their hearts they have believed in him. Nanak, they have known the one Creator.
a22.p4: The Lord's servant is attached to the Name of the one Lord, and his hope does not go in vain. To the servant, service comes naturally; understanding Hukam, God's will, he attains the supreme state. There is no thought higher than this for one in whose mind the Formless Lord dwells. Breaking their bonds, they have become free of enmity; night and day they worship the Guru's feet. They are happy in this world and at ease in the world hereafter. Nanak, the Lord God himself has united them with himself.
a22.p5: Join the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy, and rejoice; sing the praises of God, the supreme bliss. Reflect on the essence of the Lord's Name, and redeem this body so hard to obtain. Sing the Lord's praises, words of nectar; this is the way for the soul to cross over. At all hours see God near you; ignorance will end and darkness be destroyed. Hear the teaching and enshrine it in your heart. Nanak, you will receive the fruit your heart desires.
a22.p6: Set right both this life and the life hereafter: keep the Lord's Name enshrined deep in your heart. The teaching of the perfect Guru is perfect; one in whose mind it dwells has recognised the Truth. With mind and body repeat the Naam, God's Name, attuned to him in love; pain, suffering and fear will leave the mind. Trader, deal in the true trade, and your cargo will come safely through to the Lord's Court. Within your mind keep the One alone as your support. Nanak, you will not come and go again.
a22.p7: Where can anyone go far from him? One is saved by meditating on the Protector. Repeating the Name of the Fearless One, all fear is erased; by God's grace a mortal is set free. One whom God protects has no pain; repeating the Naam, the mind finds peace. Anxiety goes and pride is erased; no one can equal that servant. The valiant Guru stands over his head. Nanak, his tasks are all fulfilled.
a22.p8: Perfect is the wisdom of him whose glance is nectar; seeing his sight, the world is saved. Matchless are his lotus feet; fruitful is the sight of the Lord, and beautiful his form. Blessed is his service, and his servant is accepted; he is the knower of hearts, the Supreme Being. One in whose mind he dwells is filled with joy; death does not come near him. They have become immortal and attained the immortal state, Nanak, who meditated on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat.
a23.salok: Salok. The Guru has given the eye-salve of spiritual wisdom, and the darkness of ignorance is destroyed. Through the Lord's grace I met the saint. Nanak, the mind is filled with light.
a23.p1: Ashtapadi. In the company of the saints I have seen God within; God's Name has become sweet to me. All things are within the heart of the One, though they appear in many colours and kinds. God's Name is the nectar, the nine treasures; its resting place is within the body. There is the trance of the void, and there the unstruck melody sounds, the divine music that no instrument makes; its wonder and amazement cannot be told. He alone has seen it whom God himself has shown. Nanak, that servant gains understanding.
a23.p2: The Infinite One is within, and he is without; the Lord pervades every heart. In the earth, the sky and the regions below, in all the worlds, he is the perfect sustainer. In forest, grass and mountain is the Supreme Lord; as his command is, so is every deed. He is in air, water and fire; he is present in the four corners and the ten directions. There is no place apart from him. By the Guru's grace, Nanak, find peace.
a23.p3: See him in the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis; the One is in the moon, the sun and the stars. Everyone speaks the speech of God; he himself is steady and never wavers. With all his powers he plays his play; he cannot be bought at any price, and his virtues are priceless. He whose light is in every light, that Master upholds all, woven through like warp and weft. By the Guru's grace doubt comes to an end. Nanak, in them this faith becomes firm.
a23.p4: To the saints all they behold is God; in the hearts of the saints is all righteousness. The saints hear words of good; they are merged in the Lord who pervades all. Such is the conduct of one who has known him: all that the holy one says is true. Whatever happens, he accepts it gladly; he knows God as the doer and the cause of all doing. For him God dwells within, and outside too it is he alone. Nanak, seeing his sight, all are enchanted.
a23.p5: He himself is the Truth, and all he has made is true; from that God came the whole creation. When it pleases him, he spreads out the creation; when it pleases him, he is the One alone again. His many powers cannot be grasped; whom he pleases, he unites with himself. Who can be called near, and who far? He himself is all, filling everything. One whom he himself makes aware of his presence within, Nanak, to that servant he himself gives understanding.
a23.p6: He himself is at work in all beings; through all eyes he himself is the one who sees. All creation is his body; he himself hears his own praise. The One has made coming and going a play; he has made Maya, the world's illusion, obey his command. Amid all he remains untouched; whatever is to be said, he himself says. By his command one comes, by his command one goes. Nanak, when it pleases him, he takes them back into himself.
a23.p7: Whatever comes from him is not bad; tell me, apart from him, has anyone done anything? He himself is good, and his works are excellent beyond measure; he alone knows his own heart. He himself is the Truth, and all he upholds is true; woven through and through, he is absorbed in his own creation. No one can tell his state or his extent; only if there were another like him could that one understand. All that he does is to be accepted. By the Guru's grace, Nanak, know this.
a23.p8: One who knows this has peace for ever; that God himself unites him with himself. He is wealthy, of noble family and honoured; liberated while living is the one in whose heart the Lord dwells. Blessed, blessed, blessed is the coming of that servant, by whose grace the whole world is carried across. This is the purpose of such a servant's coming: that in his company the Name comes to mind. He himself is free, and he sets the world free. Nanak bows for ever to that servant.
a24.salok: Salok. The perfect God has been worshipped, whose Name too is perfect. Nanak, the Perfect One has been found; sing the praises of the Perfect One.
a24.p1: Ashtapadi. Hear the teaching of the perfect Guru, and see the Supreme Lord close at hand. With every breath remember Gobind, and the anxiety within your mind will lift. Give up the waves of passing hopes; my mind, ask for the dust of the saints' feet. Give up self-conceit and offer your prayer; cross the ocean of fire in the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy. Fill your storehouses with the Lord's wealth. Nanak bows to the perfect Guru.
a24.p2: For well-being, happiness, poise and bliss, worship the Lord of supreme bliss in the Saadh Sangat. Ward off hell and save your soul; drink the nectar of Gobind's praises. In your heart dwell on the one all-pervading Lord, whose form is one and whose colours are many. He is Gopal, Damodar, merciful to the meek, destroyer of pain, wholly kind. Remember, remember the Naam, God's Name, again and again. Nanak, this alone is the support of the soul.
a24.p3: The words of the holy one are verses of the highest praise; they are priceless rubies and gems. Hearing them and living by them, one is saved; such a one crosses over and carries others across. Fruitful is the life, and fruitful the company, of one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's love. For him the unstruck Word of victory resounds; hearing it again and again he rejoices, and God thunders forth within him. The Lord of the world shines forth on the foreheads of the great souls. Nanak, in their company people are saved.
a24.p4: Hearing that he is able to give refuge, we have come to his refuge; in his grace God has united us with himself. Enmity has vanished, and we have become the dust of all; in the Saadh Sangat we receive the Naam, the Name of nectar. The divine Guru is well pleased, and his servant's service is fulfilled. We are kept free of household entanglements and vice, hearing the Lord's Name and repeating it with the tongue. In his kindness God has shown mercy. Nanak, our cargo has come safely through.
a24.p5: Saints, friends, sing the praise of God, with a mind alert and fixed on him alone. The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam; one in whose mind it dwells becomes a treasure-house. All his desires are fulfilled; he becomes the foremost of men, renowned in all the world. He reaches the highest place of all, and comes and goes no more. That servant departs having earned the wealth of the Lord, Nanak, who is granted it.
a24.p6: Well-being, peace, prosperity and the nine treasures; wisdom, knowledge and every spiritual power; learning, austerity, yoga and meditation on God; the highest knowledge and the most purifying bath; the four great blessings and the blossoming of the heart-lotus; living amid all and yet detached from all; beauty, insight and knowledge of the essence of reality; looking on all alike and seeing the One alone: these fruits come to that servant who speaks the Naam with his mouth, and with his mind hears the word of the Naam from Guru Nanak.
a24.p7: Whoever repeats this treasure in the mind is liberated, in every age. This Bani, the Guru's word, holds the praises of Gobind and the melody of the Naam, of which the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas speak. The Lord's Name alone is the essence of all creeds; it rests in the minds of Gobind's devotees. In the Saadh Sangat millions of sins are erased; by the saint's grace one escapes death's messenger. Those on whose foreheads God has written his grace, Nanak, come to the refuge of the holy.
a24.p8: One in whose mind it dwells, who listens to it with love, that servant remembers the Lord God. His pain of birth and death is taken away; this precious human body is redeemed at once. Spotless is his glory, and his speech is nectar; the one Name fills his mind. Pain, sickness, fear and doubt are gone; he is called holy, and his deeds are spotless. His glory rises above all. It is for these virtues, Nanak, that its name is Sukhmani, the jewel of peace.
